subject: Subsetting a data.frame and "Operation not allowed without an active reactive context"

messages.author: bda90bcea347c4f0
messages.subject: Subsetting a data.frame and "Operation not allowed without an active reactive context"
parts:
I'm using global.r to load data that's visible to ui.R. However, I'm having trouble trying to subset the data based on the input selection.
I keep getting this error: 
Error in .getReactiveEnvironment()$currentContext() : 
  Operation not allowed without an active reactive context. (You tried to do something that can only be done from inside a reactive function.)

server.R:
library(shiny)
library(ggplot2)

# Define server logic required to plot various variables against mpg
shinyServer(function(input, output) {
data <- reactive({
subset(a, pitcher == input$pitcher)
})
})

ui.R:
library(shiny)

players <- as.character(unique(a$pitcher))
names(players) <-  as.character(unique(a$pitcher_name))

# Define UI for miles per gallon application
shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(

  # Application title
  headerPanel("PitchFX Visualizer"),

  sidebarPanel(
  selectInput("pitcher", "Pitcher:", choices = c(players))
  ),

  mainPanel()
))

messages.author: 9c9b5f9c6aaa025d
messages.subject: Re: Subsetting a data.frame and "Operation not allowed without an active reactive context"
parts:
These are different meanings of "activity." Interactive mode (which has been around before Shiny) refers to the prompt (>). So, if you are playing around in the prompt and just want a quick way to see a subset of data before committing the code, then feel free to use subset. If you are committing code for production purposes, you would want use []. 

Reactivity is a term shiny uses for the purposes of interaction with the UI.
